note: Numerics diagnostics only. No timing here; nothing scores against this.

hypothesis_tested_and_FALSIFIED.claim: Inductor selects a different SDPA backend (flash / mem-efficient / math) than eager.
hypothesis_tested_and_FALSIFIED.evidence: Generated code for the attention stage calls extern_kernels.bmm twice (reinterpret_tensor + bmm), exactly as eager's torch.matmul lowers. No scaled_dot_product_attention, no _flash_attention_forward anywhere in the output code. Both matmuls are BIT-IDENTICAL to eager (max_abs 0.0000e+00) when given identical inputs. The sfdp pattern matcher does not fire (the 2-D causal mask does not match query.dim()).

stagewise_divergence_uuid_b0c05812.method: reference rewritten to return every intermediate; whole function compiled once; eager vs compiled, identical inputs (verified bitwise equal)

mechanism_1_rope_fma_contraction.triton_source_arithmetic: tmp2 = tmp0*tmp1 ; tmp20 = tmp18*tmp19 ; tmp21 = tmp2 + tmp20  (algebraically identical to eager, same association)
mechanism_1_rope_fma_contraction.residual_533_of_1048576_elements: compiled == eager but != the fp64 emulation of the fma; attributable to double rounding in the fp64 emulation, not to a different instruction
mechanism_1_rope_fma_contraction.conclusion: the AMDGPU backend contracted the FIRST multiply of (x*cos) + (rot*sin) into a single v_fma_f32, removing one rounding. Eager runs three separate ATen kernels (mul, mul, add) and rounds twice.

at_the_max_abs_diff_element.comment: the COMPILED value is the correct one; eager is 4.77e-07 wrong there

online_softmax_toggle_test_on_a_syntheti.verdict: online softmax is NOT the cause; disabling it changes nothing

mechanism_2_softmax_reduction.conclusion: Triton's exp (__ocml_expf) differs from ATen's by up to 1 ulp on 82% of elements, and Triton's block tree-reduction sums exp in a different order than ATen's. Both are ordinary rounding differences; neither is an algorithm change.

float64_cpu_golden.method: inputs generated on GPU, moved to CPU, cast to float64, reference re-run in float64 (softmax dtype=float64)
float64_cpu_golden.verdict: compiled is NOT less accurate than eager. RMS is marginally better, max_abs identical, elementwise a coin flip. Both sit ~27 ulp from the truth while the tolerance demands ~1 ulp.

side_finding_stored_golden_is_unusable.cause: scripts/gen_golden.py does torch.manual_seed(0); prepare_inputs(..., device='cpu'); scripts/runners/calibrate_tolerance.py does torch.manual_seed(0); prepare_inputs(..., device='cuda:0'). CPU and CUDA RNG streams differ, so the two runs consume entirely different random inputs.
side_finding_stored_golden_is_unusable.consequence: the recorded vs_golden for this problem compares outputs of two different random draws. It is not evidence of anything. Any problem whose inputs are type=random is affected.
